provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slacktivity's own product page as captured 2025-02-09; product_url is that Wayback capture, not the live page, because slacktivity.com/shop/2faces-polyester-slackline/ now 301s to a shop category listing (checked 2026-09-05) - hence active false. Maker's own figures: polyester, 26 mm, 55 g/m, stretch approx 7.2% at 10 kN ("comparable to Marathon PLAY"), MBS webbing batch 2020 23.7 kN, MBS of the sewn main loop 23 kN. Stretch is that single approximate point, not a measured curve. Sold only as made-up lines, not by the metre: the capture offers 80 m at 179 EUR (145 on sale) and 100 m at 225 EUR (174 on sale, out of stock), so priceMeter is the 100 m regular price divided by its length, 2.25 EUR/m; the 80 m works out to 2.24. Sale prices are not used, matching the Anima entry. That price includes the sewn terminations, which bulk webbing prices elsewhere in this file do not. The two shipping weights corroborate the stated 55 g/m exactly (4.4 kg / 80 m and 5.5 kg / 100 m). Polyester at 23.7 kN derives Not for Highline, which is right: this is a park and longline webbing, and Slacktivity does not market it for highline.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 18.4 mm × 2.5 mm, 31 g/m, MBS 39 kN, sewn-loop MBS 46 kN, WLL 13 kN, 100 % UHMWPE (HMPE) in a flat single-layer, single-zone weave. The current production batch (W26DZ, Aug 2026) measured 39.93 kN MBS and 46.85 kN sewn loop; BC restates those per batch, so the catalogue records the published nominal 39 kN. Optimum tension 1.0–4.5 kN, preferred lengths 200 m+, backup 7 % longer than the main — HMPE creeps, so a permarig main grows into that backup. ISA stretch 1.25 % @ 5 kN and 2.08 % @ 10 kN (standardised ISA method, 200 mm gauge); BC's stretch chart publishes only those two points, so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve if a full load–elongation curve is released. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Hardware compatibility is the caveat that defines this webbing: NOT compatible with any weblock (slips single-wrapped in all of them, bends the front pin from about 24 kN double-wrapped) except a MightyLock on a Van Beest 1/2" 2-tonne shackle, double-wrapped, pin side; not compatible with any webbing grip (micro grips slip at 0.2 kN, full-size at 7 kN, Wafer XL at 12 kN). Anchor it on its sewn loops, with a soft thimble under any soft connector — without one the loop loses up to 50 % of its strength. Sewn loops are Pattern 504 (160 × 16 mm, 200 stitches) sewn with Dyneema thread; naked, sleeveless loops are also offered. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.90/m, on sale at $2.61 as of 2026-09-19); cut lengths are 50 / 60 / 100 m. Woven in China; measured, cut and sewn in Colorado. Released 2026-09-17 (Shopify listing publish date). Supersedes the original Axiom (id 213), which BC's own stretch comparison now flags as legacy.

The Wing 3.5 is the ultimate all-rounder for beginners, advanced slackliners and pros. Even during your first steps on a slackline, you will notice the pleasant dynamics of this webbing. The integrated Wing technology causes the tubular edges of the slackline to adapt to the sole of your foot. With a width of 35 mm/1.4", the webbing forgives mistakes while walking. raw_payload.description:
The Matrix jumpline is the benchmark for tricklining with an extremely dynamic and powerful rebound. The unique combination of high breaking strength, high stretch and a big safety margin while pretension with high power guarantees a new quality regarding flight level and airtime and set back every other known.

The line needs to be very tight (beyond 10kN) for powerful jumplining. So far a high risk (line break, snap) was involved. Trickling with the Matrix is more safe due to the redundant tube in tube double line approach and the high break strength in absolute and relative meanings (Matrix is world leading in jumpline strength).

100% Polyamide guarantee in contrast to the known Polyester lines a pressureful dynamic without lower death point. The rich and full thrust until take-off provides pure bounce experience. The webbing width of 32mm gives better foot placement und jump precision. The great mass inertia and damping characteristic of threaded lines ensure more time and tolerance for dynamic control.

Matrix - unleash your power!

raw_payload.description: Ultralight UHMWPE longline/highline webbing at under 30 g/m. Its very low stretch makes tensioning the longest projects efficient, while the reduced 21.5 mm width cuts wind exposure and softens the edges. Available in orange or black, and also a popular lightweight backup for freestyle sets.
raw_payload.name: Tiger
raw_payload.notes: Manufacturer specs (slackhouseshop.pl): 21.5 mm flat UHMWPE, 2.5 mm thick, 29.8 g/m, MBS 30 kN, sewn-loop MBS 30 kN, WLL 8 kN, elongation 1.9 % @ 5 kN and 2.8 % @ 10 kN, backup +7 %, made in China. Sold as 50 m or 100 m sewn segments (ST loops with an integrated soft thimble by default, or flat FL loops). Not compatible with standard weblocks or with rubber-jaw grips (too slippery) — anchor via the sewn loops or a Petram Simplex-type device with a double wrap. UHMWPE melts at 140–150 °C, so friction damage develops faster than on PA/PES. Manufacturer caps service life at 5 years and advises against permanent installs as a mainline; recommended as a mainline only from ~150 m. The prose description quotes 2.4 % @ 5 kN / 2.9 % @ 10 kN — the spec table values recorded here are the manufacturer's tabulated figures. Price is per metre at the 100 m segment (13.00 PLN/m); longer orders are cheaper per metre.

Manufacturer caps service life at 5 years and advises against permanent installs as a mainline; recommended as a mainline only from ~150 m. The prose description quotes 2.4 % @ 5 kN / 2.9 % @ 10 kN — the spec table values recorded here are the manufacturer's tabulated figures. raw_payload.notes: Specs confirmed direct by Wall Ace (2026-09-10), superseding the announcement-post figures this entry was first built from: 25 mm, 36 g/m (not 27.5), MBS 27 kN. That MBS is the strength of the webbing terminated in loops - the way the product is actually sold and used - not a raw tensile figure for the band, and it is what the derived classification is computed from. Construction is a Dyneema centre with purple nylon edges. Production has stopped - the maker's own summary of this webbing and its thinner twin, Duct Tape, is "comfortable and cheap but not exactly high tech" - so active is false, and there is no product page (product_url null). The announcement post this entry was first built from, which had a first length reaching Australia and a main shipment a month out, described the end of the run rather than the start of one. raw_payload.name: Aeon
raw_payload.notes: Specs transcribed from Landcruising's own Aeon product-archive PDF (2 pages, supplied 2026-09-05); Landcruising is defunct; product_url is the archived Landcruising shop page (Wayback, Nov 2010), active false. Maker's own wording: flat webbing, 25.8 mm (1 inch), 99 % Dyneema fibers with a red contrast thread, no labels or prints, made in Germany, 37 g/m, minimum break strength 60 kN, 1.3-1.4 % elongation at 20 kN, marketed as the webbing for superlonglines and big projects. The certificate's F=f(s) diagram is crosshead travel in mm (with the slack take-up toe), not strain, so no stretch curve is derived from it. date_introduced is September 2010: the archived shop page took pre-orders and said it ships from mid-September 2010 (the PDF says "Release 2010"; the certificate puts it in production by May 2010). Price is that page's 5.95 EUR per metre.

raw_payload.description: Affordable High Tech. Amazing for big gaps and backups for freestyle. Built for the body of a bigline, or as its backup, not for the hardware-handling ends.
raw_payload.name: Axiom MK2
raw_payload.notes: Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 18.4 mm × 2.5 mm, 31 g/m, MBS 39 kN, sewn-loop MBS 46 kN, WLL 13 kN, 100 % UHMWPE (HMPE) in a flat single-layer, single-zone weave. The current production batch (W26DZ, Aug 2026) measured 39.93 kN MBS and 46.85 kN sewn loop; BC restates those per batch, so the catalogue records the published nominal 39 kN. Optimum tension 1.0–4.5 kN, preferred lengths 200 m+, backup 7 % longer than the main — HMPE creeps, so a permarig main grows into that backup. ISA stretch 1.25 % @ 5 kN and 2.08 % @ 10 kN (standardised ISA method, 200 mm gauge); BC's stretch chart publishes only those two points, so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve if a full load–elongation curve is released. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Hardware compatibility is the caveat that defines this webbing: NOT compatible with any weblock (slips single-wrapped in all of them, bends the front pin from about 24 kN double-wrapped) except a MightyLock on a Van Beest 1/2" 2-tonne shackle, double-wrapped, pin side; not compatible with any webbing grip (micro grips slip at 0.2 kN, full-size at 7 kN, Wafer XL at 12 kN). Anchor it on its sewn loops, with a soft thimble under any soft connector — without one the loop loses up to 50 % of its strength. Sewn loops are Pattern 504 (160 × 16 mm, 200 stitches) sewn with Dyneema thread; naked, sleeveless loops are also offered. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.90/m, on sale at $2.61 as of 2026-09-19); cut lengths are 50 / 60 / 100 m. Woven in China; measured, cut and sewn in Colorado. Released 2026-09-17 (Shopify listing publish date). Supersedes the original Axiom (id 213), which BC's own stretch comparison now flags as legacy.

raw_payload.description:
The original webbing that must not be named that has been sold in the "slackshop that must not be named" store before. We found the last pieces of it and make them available for you at a very special price! We take the liberty to quote portions of the text that a former German "slackshop that must not be named" used to describe this webbing: "The webbing that must not be named" - this was the reference amongst allround slackline webbings back in 2016 and the "slackshop that must not be named" masterpiece. This webbing came with lots of innovative details back then. Its perfectly designed features still allow you to push the limits today. The high stretch version offers an extended stretch and is especially suitable for more dynamic applications like bouncy longlines while it's still easy to tension. The higher stretch absorbs impact forces more effectively in the case of shock loads. The webbing which must not be named - no limits!"

Note: this is Landcruising's [Core 2 HS](/webbings/1), resold by Raed under another name.
raw_payload.name: TWTMNBN (The Webbing That Must Not Be Named)
raw_payload.notes: Raed's end-of-stock resale of Landcruising's Core 2 HS (id 1) under its old nickname - Landcruising's former shop (slackshop.de, "the slackshop that must not be named") sold Core 2 as "the webbing that must not be named". Raed's page quotes that shop's copy: 2016, flat polyester kernmantle (core + sheath), SoftEdge, dual colour blue/yellow with black edges, high-stretch version, average MBS 44 kN, 7 % at 13 kN, 71.5 g/m, made in Germany - every figure matches the Core 2 HS row, so its thickness (3.5 mm) and stretch curve are copied from row 1. Raed's spec table: 25 mm, 6 % stretch at 1/3 MBS, optimised for highlines/longlines/waterlines, cut lengths 75/100/150/200 m; the product graphic says 6 % / 72 g/m / 45 kN, core/sheath, Hydro Shield, Therma Stretch, Soft Edge. Raed notes it was factory heat treated and is stiff when new. Price is the regular EUR 2.20/m incl. 19 % VAT (on sale at 1.54) from the Wayback capture of 2019-10-18; the live page is gone and the stock was 'the last pieces', so active is false.

Unicorn is the new all-round slackline by Landcruising. We have placed special emphasis on safety, comfort and pleasant walking characteristics. Based on the webbing design of Core 2, we have implemented a new innovative edge design, which provides a distinctly noticeable softness. The so-called Soft-Cushion padding is located on both edges of the line and provides a significantly softer haptic under the sole of the foot. Specs transcribed from Landcruising's own Aeon product-archive PDF (2 pages, supplied 2026-09-05); Landcruising is defunct; product_url is the archived Landcruising shop page (Wayback, Nov 2010), active false. Maker's own wording: flat webbing, 25.8 mm (1 inch), 99 % Dyneema fibers with a red contrast thread, no labels or prints, made in Germany, 37 g/m, minimum break strength 60 kN, 1.3-1.4 % elongation at 20 kN, marketed as the webbing for superlonglines and big projects. The certificate's F=f(s) diagram is crosshead travel in mm (with the slack take-up toe), not strain, so no stretch curve is derived from it. date_introduced is September 2010: the archived shop page took pre-orders and said it ships from mid-September 2010 (the PDF says "Release 2010"; the certificate puts it in production by May 2010). Price is that page's 5.95 EUR per metre.

Specs from Slacktivity's own product page as captured 2025-02-09; product_url is that Wayback capture, not the live page, because slacktivity.com/shop/2faces-polyester-slackline/ now 301s to a shop category listing (checked 2026-09-05) - hence active false. Maker's own figures: polyester, 26 mm, 55 g/m, stretch approx 7.2% at 10 kN ("comparable to Marathon PLAY"), MBS webbing batch 2020 23.7 kN, MBS of the sewn main loop 23 kN. Sold only as made-up lines, not by the metre: the capture offers 80 m at 179 EUR (145 on sale) and 100 m at 225 EUR (174 on sale, out of stock), so priceMeter is the 100 m regular price divided by its length, 2.25 EUR/m; the 80 m works out to 2.24. The two shipping weights corroborate the stated 55 g/m exactly (4.4 kg / 80 m and 5.5 kg / 100 m). Polyester at 23.7 kN derives Not for Highline, which is right: this is a park and longline webbing, and Slacktivity does not market it for highline.

source.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#261 (Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters / Axiom MK2)
source.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 18.4 mm × 2.5 mm, 31 g/m, MBS 39 kN, sewn-loop MBS 46 kN, WLL 13 kN, 100 % UHMWPE (HMPE) in a flat single-layer, single-zone weave. The current production batch (W26DZ, Aug 2026) measured 39.93 kN MBS and 46.85 kN sewn loop; BC restates those per batch, so the catalogue records the published nominal 39 kN. Optimum tension 1.0–4.5 kN, preferred lengths 200 m+, backup 7 % longer than the main — HMPE creeps, so a permarig main grows into that backup. ISA stretch 1.25 % @ 5 kN and 2.08 % @ 10 kN (standardised ISA method, 200 mm gauge); BC's stretch chart publishes only those two points, so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve if a full load–elongation curve is released. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Hardware compatibility is the caveat that defines this webbing: NOT compatible with any weblock (slips single-wrapped in all of them, bends the front pin from about 24 kN double-wrapped) except a MightyLock on a Van Beest 1/2" 2-tonne shackle, double-wrapped, pin side; not compatible with any webbing grip (micro grips slip at 0.2 kN, full-size at 7 kN, Wafer XL at 12 kN). Anchor it on its sewn loops, with a soft thimble under any soft connector — without one the loop loses up to 50 % of its strength. Sewn loops are Pattern 504 (160 × 16 mm, 200 stitches) sewn with Dyneema thread; naked, sleeveless loops are also offered. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.90/m, on sale at $2.61 as of 2026-09-19); cut lengths are 50 / 60 / 100 m. Woven in China; measured, cut and sewn in Colorado. Released 2026-09-17 (Shopify listing publish date). Supersedes the original Axiom (id 213), which BC's own stretch comparison now flags as legacy.

source.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slack.fr's own shop page as captured 2014-08-29; product_url is that Wayback capture, because shop.slack.fr is long gone (Slack.fr's catalogue is now carried by Slack Inov) - hence active false. The capture confirms, unchanged, the four figures this row already held from the SlackDB import: flat, 100 % polyester, 25 mm, 62 g/m, MBS 28 kN. Two things it adds. (1) Elongation: the maker states 5.5 % at 15 kN, recorded as a second stretch point beside the inherited 4.7 % at 10 kN - two single quoted figures, not a measured curve. (2) Price: the shop sells three lengths, 25 m at 49 EUR, 50 m at 79 EUR and 100 m at 145 EUR, i.e. 1.96, 1.58 and 1.45 EUR/m. priceMeter was 1.96, which is exactly the 25 m tier - the dearest per metre of the three. It is set here to 1.45, the 100 m line this capture is the page for, matching the 2FACES entry's rule of taking the longest length's regular price; the ladder is recorded above so the other tiers are not lost. Prices include the made-up line, not bulk webbing by the metre. The maker calls the product Superflat "Dark Blue"; the catalogue name stays "Dark Blue" because the id and name are already recorded elsewhere. Polyester at 28 kN derives Type B.

provenance.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#263 (Raed Slacklines / TWTMNBN (The Webbing That Must Not Be Named))
provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Raed's end-of-stock resale of Landcruising's Core 2 HS (id 1) under its old nickname - Landcruising's former shop (slackshop.de, "the slackshop that must not be named") sold Core 2 as "the webbing that must not be named". Raed's page quotes that shop's copy: 2016, flat polyester kernmantle (core + sheath), SoftEdge, dual colour blue/yellow with black edges, high-stretch version, average MBS 44 kN, 7 % at 13 kN, 71.5 g/m, made in Germany - every figure matches the Core 2 HS row, so its thickness (3.5 mm) and stretch curve are copied from row 1. Raed's spec table: 25 mm, 6 % stretch at 1/3 MBS, optimised for highlines/longlines/waterlines, cut lengths 75/100/150/200 m; the product graphic says 6 % / 72 g/m / 45 kN, core/sheath, Hydro Shield, Therma Stretch, Soft Edge. Raed notes it was factory heat treated and is stiff when new. Price is the regular EUR 2.20/m incl. 19 % VAT (on sale at 1.54) from the Wayback capture of 2019-10-18; the live page is gone and the stock was 'the last pieces', so active is false.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slacklife BC's own product page (Wayback, 2017-10-08): MBS 35.6 kN (8000 lbs), WLL 7.12 kN (1600 lbs), 35 g/m, price 8.99 CAD/m (also sold by the foot, and in 50-1000 m lengths), colour red and white, designed and made 100% in Canada, continuous lengths over 1000 m. The page gives stretch only as "1-4%" with no load, so no stretch curve is recorded. A second Slacklife BC webbing, "HighTech" (#137: 48 g/m, 39.2 kN, 4.6% @ 10 kN, carried over from SlackDB), was a mistake: it is this same product, whose page titles it "Lion Line - Hightech Webbing". Confirmed with the Mayor of Squamish. #137 was removed on 2026-10-08 and its figures discarded, not merged; its id is not reused.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. One row for Landcruising's 25 mm Verve, merged on 2026-10-07 from #151 'Verve 25mm' and the staged 'Verve 25mm Red'. Specs, price and description from the red Verve page (Wayback 2011-07-22): PES flat, MBS 31 kN, 7 % at 10 kN, 58 g/m, max. 10 kN pretension as a longline, made in Germany, 1.49 €/m (1.40 €/m from 100 m). provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs confirmed direct by Wall Ace (2026-09-10), superseding the announcement-post figures this entry was first built from: 25 mm, 36 g/m (not 27.5), MBS 27 kN. That MBS is the strength of the webbing terminated in loops - the way the product is actually sold and used - not a raw tensile figure for the band, and it is what the derived classification is computed from. Construction is a Dyneema centre with purple nylon edges. Production has stopped - the maker's own summary of this webbing and its thinner twin, Duct Tape, is "comfortable and cheap but not exactly high tech" - so active is false, and there is no product page (product_url null). The announcement post this entry was first built from, which had a first length reaching Australia and a main shipment a month out, described the end of the run rather than the start of one. Sizing: sold only as a complete highline kit, and always in the same two segments - a 75 m main and an 83 m backup (4 loops included), at an indicative, not-yet-finalised ~580 AUD for the kit. No priceMeter is recorded: `price` on a webbing is per metre, and dividing an unfinalised kit price by 158 m would invent a number the maker has not quoted. Stretch is recorded as null, deliberately. The maker's own account is that it is very hard to put one figure on: roughly 5% between 1 and 3 kN, then about 2.5% more between 3 and 5 kN - so on the order of 7.5% total at 5 kN - with the curve flattening off as load climbs further. That is a shape described from memory, not a measured curve, and the earlier single 2.5% at 5 kN point taken from the announcement post was wrong by a factor of three. A wrong curve on a chart is worse than no curve. Photos: the two Wall Ace webbing images we hold are shared between Steel Cable and Duct Tape. The products are the same weave in two thicknesses, and the maker's own view is that the same picture serves both - and that the one filed under Steel Cable may in fact be Duct Tape. Which image is which is not settled.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs transcribed from Landcruising's own Aeon product-archive PDF (2 pages, supplied 2026-09-05); Landcruising is defunct; product_url is the archived Landcruising shop page (Wayback, Nov 2010), active false. Maker's own wording: flat webbing, 25.8 mm (1 inch), 99 % Dyneema fibers with a red contrast thread, no labels or prints, made in Germany, 37 g/m, minimum break strength 60 kN, 1.3-1.4 % elongation at 20 kN, marketed as the webbing for superlonglines and big projects. Page 2 is the mill's tensile certificate (Gurtband-Zertifikat, 26.05.2010, n = 1, KMW 100 kN): break force 6385 daN (63.85 kN), elongation 1.37 % at 20 kN, thickness 2.80 mm, width 25.8 mm - those measured figures are the source for thickness and for the single 1.37 % / 20 kN stretch point. breakingStrength records the stated 60 kN minimum, not the 63.85 kN of that one specimen. The certificate's F=f(s) diagram is crosshead travel in mm (with the slack take-up toe), not strain, so no stretch curve is derived from it. date_introduced is September 2010: the archived shop page took pre-orders and said it ships from mid-September 2010 (the PDF says "Release 2010"; the certificate puts it in production by May 2010). Price is that page's 5.95 EUR per metre.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Sterling's own product page (checked 2026-09-05). It is a rigging/rescue webbing, not a slackline product: the page publishes exactly one number, MBS 9,800 lb / 43.5 kN, and no weight, thickness or elongation figure exists to record - hence the nulls. Width is the 1" nominal, carried as 25.4 mm like the other imperial webbings (the loader truncates it to the model's int mm). priceMeter is DERIVED, not quoted: the only length sold is a 150 ft web wheel at 163.99 USD, and 163.99 / 45.72 m = 3.59 USD/m. Sterling rounds the wheel to "46 m" on the page, which would give 3.57; the exact conversion of 150 ft is used here. Nylon at 43.5 kN derives classification A+, but nothing about this webbing is ISA-certified or marketed for highline.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slacktivity's own product page as captured 2025-02-09; product_url is that Wayback capture, not the live page, because slacktivity.com/shop/2faces-polyester-slackline/ now 301s to a shop category listing (checked 2026-09-05) - hence active false. Maker's own figures: polyester, 26 mm, 55 g/m, stretch approx 7.2% at 10 kN ("comparable to Marathon PLAY"), MBS webbing batch 2020 23.7 kN, MBS of the sewn main loop 23 kN. Stretch is that single approximate point, not a measured curve. Sold only as made-up lines, not by the metre: the capture offers 80 m at 179 EUR (145 on sale) and 100 m at 225 EUR (174 on sale, out of stock), so priceMeter is the 100 m regular price divided by its length, 2.25 EUR/m; the 80 m works out to 2.24. Sale prices are not used, matching the Anima entry. That price includes the sewn terminations, which bulk webbing prices elsewhere in this file do not. The two shipping weights corroborate the stated 55 g/m exactly (4.4 kg / 80 m and 5.5 kg / 100 m). Polyester at 23.7 kN derives Not for Highline, which is right: this is a park and longline webbing, and Slacktivity does not market it for highline.

products.name: Duct Tape

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs direct from Wall Ace (2026-09-10), the only source - there is no product page. In the maker's words this is exactly the same webbing as their Steel Cable, just thinner: the same 25 mm Dyneema-centre, nylon-edge weave, at 27 g/m with an MBS of 13 kN. As with Steel Cable that MBS is the looped, terminated strength rather than a raw tensile figure. Production has stopped, as it has for Steel Cable - the maker's own summary of both is "comfortable and cheap but not exactly high tech", which is why - so active is false. Sizing: sold only as a complete highline kit, and always in the same two segments - a 75 m main and an 83 m backup (4 loops included), at an indicative, not-yet-finalised ~580 AUD for the kit. No priceMeter is recorded: `price` on a webbing is per metre, and dividing an unfinalised kit price by 158 m would invent a number the maker has not quoted. Stretch is recorded as null, deliberately. The maker's own account is that it is very hard to put one figure on: roughly 5% between 1 and 3 kN, then about 2.5% more between 3 and 5 kN - so on the order of 7.5% total at 5 kN - with the curve flattening off as load climbs further. That is a shape described from memory, not a measured curve, and the earlier single 2.5% at 5 kN point taken from the announcement post was wrong by a factor of three. A wrong curve on a chart is worse than no curve. Photos: the two Wall Ace webbing images we hold are shared between Steel Cable and Duct Tape. The products are the same weave in two thicknesses, and the maker's own view is that the same picture serves both - and that the one filed under Steel Cable may in fact be Duct Tape. Which image is which is not settled.

products.name: Axiom MK2

provenance.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#261 (Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters / Axiom MK2)
provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 18.4 mm × 2.5 mm, 31 g/m, MBS 39 kN, sewn-loop MBS 46 kN, WLL 13 kN, 100 % UHMWPE (HMPE) in a flat single-layer, single-zone weave. The current production batch (W26DZ, Aug 2026) measured 39.93 kN MBS and 46.85 kN sewn loop; BC restates those per batch, so the catalogue records the published nominal 39 kN. Optimum tension 1.0–4.5 kN, preferred lengths 200 m+, backup 7 % longer than the main — HMPE creeps, so a permarig main grows into that backup. ISA stretch 1.25 % @ 5 kN and 2.08 % @ 10 kN (standardised ISA method, 200 mm gauge); BC's stretch chart publishes only those two points, so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve if a full load–elongation curve is released. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Hardware compatibility is the caveat that defines this webbing: NOT compatible with any weblock (slips single-wrapped in all of them, bends the front pin from about 24 kN double-wrapped) except a MightyLock on a Van Beest 1/2" 2-tonne shackle, double-wrapped, pin side; not compatible with any webbing grip (micro grips slip at 0.2 kN, full-size at 7 kN, Wafer XL at 12 kN). Anchor it on its sewn loops, with a soft thimble under any soft connector — without one the loop loses up to 50 % of its strength. Sewn loops are Pattern 504 (160 × 16 mm, 200 stitches) sewn with Dyneema thread; naked, sleeveless loops are also offered. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.90/m, on sale at $2.61 as of 2026-09-19); cut lengths are 50 / 60 / 100 m. Woven in China; measured, cut and sewn in Colorado. Released 2026-09-17 (Shopify listing publish date). Supersedes the original Axiom (id 213), which BC's own stretch comparison now flags as legacy.

provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Specs from Slack.fr's own shop page as captured 2014-08-29; product_url is that Wayback capture, because shop.slack.fr is long gone (Slack.fr's catalogue is now carried by Slack Inov) - hence active false. The capture confirms, unchanged, the four figures this row already held from the SlackDB import: flat, 100 % polyester, 25 mm, 62 g/m, MBS 28 kN. Two things it adds. (1) Elongation: the maker states 5.5 % at 15 kN, recorded as a second stretch point beside the inherited 4.7 % at 10 kN - two single quoted figures, not a measured curve. (2) Price: the shop sells three lengths, 25 m at 49 EUR, 50 m at 79 EUR and 100 m at 145 EUR, i.e. 1.96, 1.58 and 1.45 EUR/m. priceMeter was 1.96, which is exactly the 25 m tier - the dearest per metre of the three. It is set here to 1.45, the 100 m line this capture is the page for, matching the 2FACES entry's rule of taking the longest length's regular price; the ladder is recorded above so the other tiers are not lost. Prices include the made-up line, not bulk webbing by the metre. The maker calls the product Superflat "Dark Blue"; the catalogue name stays "Dark Blue" because the id and name are already recorded elsewhere. Polyester at 28 kN derives Type B.

provenance.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#242 (Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters / Paradigm MK2)
provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 25.0 mm × 2.44 mm, 49.0 g/m, MBS 25 kN, sewn-loop MBS 23 kN, WLL 8 kN, 100 % nylon (polyamide) tubular weave with coloured edges, single zone. Optimum tension 1.8–2.2 kN, preferred lengths 15–100 m, backup 18 % longer than the main. Holding strengths: Alpine WebLock 24 kN, MightyLock 23 kN. ISA stretch 11.5 % @ 5 kN and 17.5 % @ 10 kN — BC states the full stretch chart is 'coming soon', so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve once released-product data is published. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.40/m); cut lengths run 40–100 m. Released 2026-07-23 (Shopify listing publish date).

provenance.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#254 (Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters / Spider Silk MK1)
provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. The first of the Spider Silk line. Balance Community's product page (checked 2026-09-05) carries nothing but "Legacy product, no longer for sale", a 5.00 USD price and a sold-out button - its "View Specs" section is empty, and the Shopify product JSON adds nothing - so width and price are the whole record and everything else is genuinely unknown, not un-transcribed. materialType is "Other" for that reason: the rest of the line is Vectran (MK2), Vectran + Dyneema (MK3), Dyneema + polyester (MK4) and Vectran + polyester (MK5), so the family does not settle what MK1 was woven from, and `material` is NOT NULL in the model. Width 25 mm and 5.00 USD/m as supplied by the operator and confirmed on the page.

provenance.citation: data/materials/webbings.json#261 (Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters / Axiom MK2)
provenance.note: Supplied offline evidence; URL not verified by importer. Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): 18.4 mm × 2.5 mm, 31 g/m, MBS 39 kN, sewn-loop MBS 46 kN, WLL 13 kN, 100 % UHMWPE (HMPE) in a flat single-layer, single-zone weave. The current production batch (W26DZ, Aug 2026) measured 39.93 kN MBS and 46.85 kN sewn loop; BC restates those per batch, so the catalogue records the published nominal 39 kN. Optimum tension 1.0–4.5 kN, preferred lengths 200 m+, backup 7 % longer than the main — HMPE creeps, so a permarig main grows into that backup. ISA stretch 1.25 % @ 5 kN and 2.08 % @ 10 kN (standardised ISA method, 200 mm gauge); BC's stretch chart publishes only those two points, so REVISIT and replace this two-point curve if a full load–elongation curve is released. BC labels it highline-approved; that is the maker's own statement, not an ISA certification. Hardware compatibility is the caveat that defines this webbing: NOT compatible with any weblock (slips single-wrapped in all of them, bends the front pin from about 24 kN double-wrapped) except a MightyLock on a Van Beest 1/2" 2-tonne shackle, double-wrapped, pin side; not compatible with any webbing grip (micro grips slip at 0.2 kN, full-size at 7 kN, Wafer XL at 12 kN). Anchor it on its sewn loops, with a soft thimble under any soft connector — without one the loop loses up to 50 % of its strength. Sewn loops are Pattern 504 (160 × 16 mm, 200 stitches) sewn with Dyneema thread; naked, sleeveless loops are also offered. Price is the custom per-metre rate ($2.90/m, on sale at $2.61 as of 2026-09-19); cut lengths are 50 / 60 / 100 m. Woven in China; measured, cut and sewn in Colorado. Released 2026-09-17 (Shopify listing publish date). Supersedes the original Axiom (id 213), which BC's own stretch comparison now flags as legacy.
